title: Marketplace canary + fallback playbook (wip)
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact playbook to run a staggered marketplace listing launch using canary traffic routing + automated fallback. Target audience: product, listing owners, technical PMs, SRE/ops and partner success. Goal is to make the listing go-live predictable and reversible with minimal customer impact.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Redwood-hosted listing tiles and publisher integrations on AWS Marketplace, Azure Marketplace, and GCP Marketplace.
- Assumes listing artifacts (tile copy, screenshots, SKU mapping) are already provisioned in vendor portals.
- We will run a traffic-based canary (real customers directed via marketplace routing or internal proxy) and monitor key signals for 72 hours.

High-level rollout objective:
- Validate billing/entitlement flow, provisioning webhook paths, and support routing at low risk.
- Maintain error budget <2% for critical flows during canary window.
- Provide immediate automated rollback/fallback if threshold breaches.

Canary traffic schedule (recommended):
- Step 0: Dry-run no-customer smoke (internal tenant + manual tests) — 0% external traffic — 1–3 hours.
- Step 1: Micro canary — 0.5% traffic (or 5 users) — 30–60 min.
- Step 2: Small canary — 5% traffic — 2 hours.
- Step 3: Ramp — 25% traffic — 6 hours.
- Step 4: Full launch — 100% traffic (unless blocked) — monitor 72h.
Notes: If marketplace routing can't do exact percentages, prefer absolute sessions/users and use feature flags + proxy layer to route.

Automated triggers and rollback criteria (fail-fast):
- Critical errors: any successful provisioning attempts failing to create tenant or license >1% of canary requests for 15min -> immediate rollback to previous offer.
- Latency/backpressure: p95 API latency growth >2x baseline for 15min -> pause ramp and investigate.
- Billing mismatch: any mapping error causing wrong SKU assignment or 401/403 from vendor APIs for >0.5% of attempts -> rollback.
- Support spike: inbound support tickets from marketplace channel >3x baseline in 30min -> pause and triage.
- Data leak/security: any sensitive payload observed in logs or alerts from DLP/KMS -> immediate takedown and incident path.

Monitoring KPIs and dashboards to stand up before canary:
- Provisioning success rate (per-minute) — golden signal.
- API latency p50/p95/p99 per route.
- Marketplace billing events vs. expected mapping (delta metric).
- Errors by code (4xx/5xx) segmented by vendor and region.
- Support intake volume (marketplace channel).
- Cost unit rate — tokens/requests cost should not spike unexpectedly.
- Logs: failed webhooks, retry loops, auth/permission errors.
- Traces: sampling on provision/login flows.

Acceptance checklist (pre-canary):
- Legal: EULA and partner terms uploaded and signed.
- Security: Threat model reviewed, KMS keys mapped, SSO OIDC config validated.
- Billing: SKU mapping document signed off and verified in sandbox with 10 synthetic transactions.
- Observability: dashboards live, alerts wired to on-call channel and mobile.
- Support: playbook for first-line support, escalation contacts listed, webhook re-delivery policy documented.
- Operations: rollback runbook live + automation in CI to flip feature flag / route.
- Docs: listing help center article drafts and troubleshooting FAQ published in staging.

Listing copy variants (short tests for tile + tooltip + short description):
- Variant A (concise):
  Title: Redwood Inference — Hosted LLM inference API
  One-liner: Low-latency LLM inference with predictable SLAs and usage-based pricing.
  Short bullets: High throughput, model catalog, secure VPC options.
- Variant B (value-focused):
  Title: Production LLM Serving for Engineering Teams
  One-liner: Ship LLM features faster — predictable latency, cost controls, and enterprise tooling.
  Short bullets: Dedicated capacity, audit logs, rollout controls.
- Variant C (developer-first):
  Title: Developer-friendly LLM Inference Platform
  One-liner: Simple API, streaming, and SDKs with deployment flexibility (hosted, dedicated, private).
  Short bullets: Quickstart code, sample prompts, metrics.
Testing note: run A/B test during ramp (50/50) at Step 2 and compare click-to-provision conversion and support tickets.

Fallback messaging templates (when listing is paused or rolled back):
- Public customer-facing tile notice: "Temporarily paused for updates — our team is applying fixes to improve provisioning reliability. We expect service to resume shortly. For urgent needs contact support@redwood.ai."
- Marketplace internal note for vendor portal (ops): "Canary paused due to provisioning failures at t+1h. Rolling back routing and disabling new provision attempts. See incident MKP-8901."

Launch simulator (mini-scenario to run before step 0):
1) Create 10 synthetic customers via staging marketplace API (all vendor portals if possible).
2) Trigger normal provisioning flow and verify: webhook delivery, tenant create, entitlement grant, first API token issue, and initial cost meter event.
3) Simulate transient failure: return 503 on webhook endpoint and verify our retry/backoff behaves and we surface an alert.
4) Simulate billing mismatch by mapping SKU->plan incorrectly in staging and confirm alerting and rollback path.
5) Run smoke load for 1 minute at 2x expected per-tenant token rate and ensure p95 latency below SLA threshold.
Expected outputs: runbook steps executed, alerts fired in expected channels, and automated rollback test toggled successfully.

Post-launch evaluation (72h):
- Run daily readout with metrics: provisioning success rate, billing reconciliation delta, support tickets, churn signal for first-week trials.
- Mark any feature flags to be kept for progressive rollout vs turned off based on observed stability.
- Capture learnings in a single readout doc and update this playbook (owner updates within 7 days).

Open questions / decisions to resolve before canary:
- Do we prefer vendor-level routing (marketplace-provided) or in-path feature flagging for percentage splits? Pros/cons summary required from infra.
- SLA messaging: what exact p95 number we advertise on the tile at launch vs. what we internally aim for?
- Who will own the first 6-hour on-call window after full launch (rotation specifics)?

Appendix: quick command checklist (ops)
- Toggle feature flag: infra-cfg feature marketplace_listing_<ID> -> on/off
- Reset provisioning queue: redis-cli FLUSHKEYS marketplace:provision:<ID>
- Force rollback: api POST /internal/marketplace/rollbacks {listing_id, reason}

Notes and provenance:
- This is a working draft — expect iterations after a dry run.
- Related materials: billing SKU mapping spreadsheet (linked), vendor portal screenshots, support playbook (linked).

Owner and next steps:
- Owner: Asha Patel (product marketing / go-to-market).
- Action: schedule dry-run with infra and solutions engineering, aim for canary window in next release sprint.

Document history: created 2025-11-12; draft updates 2026-02-28 (added billing mismatch trigger and launch simulator steps).
